skill: Plan and protect the 40-hour week
what_good_looks_like: Each Monday sets a week plan around the 1:1-agreed top 3, blocks self-study, Anki and documentation time as in docs/05-time-management.md, and flags any slip to the Manager by Wednesday.

skill: Ask good questions
what_good_looks_like: Searches the primers, glossary and OneNote for 15 minutes first, logs each question with context, what was checked and a proposed answer, and turns reusable answers into a card, glossary entry or SOP line within 2 working days.

skill: Keep own work visible in Jira
what_good_looks_like: Every piece of own work has a Jira item with a clear title, acceptance criteria and a status updated at least twice a week, and active work stays within the agreed work-in-progress limit.

skill: Write clear status updates for stakeholders
what_good_looks_like: Writes Friday self-reports and stakeholder updates that lead with the answer and state impact, dates, risks and asks, and they go out without the Manager rewriting them.

skill: Capture knowledge as reviewed docs and Anki cards
what_good_looks_like: Turns sessions, shadowing and answered questions into OneNote pages, SOP lines and company-specific Anki cards with a Draft, Reviewed or Published status, and the cards pass the milestone spot check with zero factual errors.

skill: Deliver a teach-back
what_good_looks_like: Explains a topic in 15 minutes using docs/templates/knowledge/teach-back.md, answers follow-up questions without notes, and says what they do not know instead of guessing.

skill: Explain the business and its stakeholders
what_good_looks_like: Without notes, explains what we import, from where and into which countries, and keeps a 1-page stakeholder map showing what each group needs from the team and how tariff and cost news reaches them.

skill: Explain the life of a US import entry and who does what
what_good_looks_like: Without notes, walks through release, entry summary (CBP Form 7501), duty payment, liquidation and the protest window, and states what the importer of record, the licensed broker and CBP each own.

skill: Explain the Canada and Mexico import processes
what_good_looks_like: Explains the CBSA flow (release, CARM, Commercial Accounting Declaration, BN/RM account) and the Mexico flow (agente aduanal, pedimento, padrón de importadores, IVA), and names the data our team provides to each broker.

skill: Classify an item using the GRIs
what_good_looks_like: Classifies a new item to 6-digit HS with written GRI reasoning backed by section and chapter notes, Explanatory Notes and CROSS rulings, finds the national line in the HTSUS, the Canada Customs Tariff and TIGIE, and flags doubtful cases for review.

skill: Calculate duties and fees for an entry line
what_good_looks_like: For an entry line, identifies the value basis, the rate column (general, USMCA or other preference, Chapter 99 additional duties) and fees such as MPF and HMF, and recomputes the duty to the cent or explains the difference.

skill: Apply USMCA rules of origin and certification
what_good_looks_like: Tests an item against its product-specific rule (tariff shift, RVC, de minimis) using its bill of materials, checks a certification for the nine minimum data elements, and states the importer's obligations if the claim fails.

skill: Explain Mexico IMMEX, Anexo 24 and Anexo 31
what_good_looks_like: Explains what an IMMEX temporary import defers, what Anexo 24 inventory control and Anexo 31 credit tracking require, and which of our trade data feeds them [COMPANY: confirm IMMEX scope].

skill: Audit a broker filing against our data
what_good_looks_like: Compares a filed entry line (HTS, value, origin, preference claim, duty) with our item master and PO or invoice data, logs each discrepancy with evidence, and routes it to the right owner.

skill: Recognize and escalate a compliance issue
what_good_looks_like: Spots a potential error in classification, value or origin, documents the facts, and escalates to the Senior or Manager the same day without contacting the broker or a government agency about corrections on their own.

skill: Explain GTM concepts and map AS400 functions to e2open
what_good_looks_like: Explains the core GTM functions (product classification, origin and trade agreements, screening, landed cost, customs filing data) and maps each AS400 trade function we use to the e2open concept that will replace it.

skill: Trace trade data end to end
what_good_looks_like: Draws from memory how trade data flows from the AS400 item and classification master through Oracle, broker exchange, SQL Server and the data warehouse to reports, and names at least 3 points where data quality breaks.

skill: Look up an item's trade data in AS400
what_good_looks_like: Finds an item's classification, origin, program flags and rates in the AS400 trade system (inquiry only) or its warehouse copy, and explains any mismatch between the two.

skill: Explain Oracle touchpoints for trade data
what_good_looks_like: Explains which trade data Oracle receives or sends for items, purchase orders, receipts and cost, and shows where duty, freight and fees enter [COMPANY: Oracle EBS or Fusion] cost data.

skill: Explain and check broker data exchange
what_good_looks_like: Explains what data goes to each country's broker and what entry data comes back, by which method and how often [COMPANY: broker interfaces], and reconciles a returned file against our master data.

skill: Query SQL Server and the warehouse with SQL
what_good_looks_like: Writes readable T-SQL with joins, filters, aggregation, CTEs and window functions, checks row counts after every join, and saves each query with a header comment stating purpose, source and author.

skill: Navigate the data warehouse
what_good_looks_like: Finds the right table or view for a question, states its grain, keys and refresh timing, and knows which fields come from AS400, Oracle or broker files.

skill: Shape data in Excel and Power Query
what_good_looks_like: Builds a refreshable Power Query that imports, cleans, merges and pivots an extract, with named steps a reviewer can follow and no manual edits after refresh.

skill: Use and build Power BI reports
what_good_looks_like: Traces a report visual to its semantic model and measure, builds a simple page with DAX measures, and explains why a Power BI number differs from an Excel extract.

skill: Validate and present an analysis
what_good_looks_like: Reconciles results to a control total, lists assumptions and caveats, and writes a 1-page findings memo that the reviewer signs off with no material errors.

skill: Run intake and scope a request
what_good_looks_like: Runs an intake conversation, completes docs/templates/bsa/01-intake-request.md, and creates a Jira item with problem, impact, scope and acceptance criteria that the requester confirms.

skill: Write testable requirements and user stories
what_good_looks_like: Writes requirements and user stories with acceptance criteria and MoSCoW priority (docs/templates/bsa/02-requirements.md and 07-jira-epic-story.md) that a tester could test without asking questions.

skill: Document an as-is process
what_good_looks_like: Documents an as-is process with steps, roles, systems, inputs, outputs, controls and pain points in docs/templates/bsa/03-process-map-as-is-to-be.md, and the process owner confirms it is accurate.

skill: Write a data mapping spec
what_good_looks_like: Maps each source field to its target with type, rules, transformations and data-quality notes in docs/templates/bsa/04-data-mapping-spec.md, and the reviewer finds no unmapped required field.

skill: Plan and run UAT
what_good_looks_like: Writes UAT cases with expected results traced to requirements (docs/templates/bsa/05-uat-test-plan.md), runs them, logs defects with reproduction steps, and records business sign-off.

skill: Take a change through change control
what_good_looks_like: Raises a change request with impact, test evidence, rollback plan and checker review (docs/templates/bsa/06-change-request.md) before anything moves to production.

skill: Find and read primary sources
what_good_looks_like: Within 60 minutes finds and reads the controlling sources for a new action (Federal Register notice and annexes, proclamation or executive order, CBP CSMS, HTSUS Chapter 99, CBSA customs notices, DOF) and monitors them for changes.

skill: Determine the legal scope of a tariff action
what_good_looks_like: States affected HTS codes, countries of origin, rates, effective and end dates, exclusions and in-transit rules with a citation for each, and matches the HTS list to our item master.

skill: Interpret stacking and exclusions
what_good_looks_like: Works out which Chapter 99 provisions and other measures apply together to an item and how they interact with USMCA claims, and writes the interpretation with sources for checker review.

skill: Write a Tariff-Impact Brief
what_good_looks_like: Completes docs/templates/domain/tariff-impact-brief.md with a primary source for every claim, open questions flagged and no dollar conclusions, and the checker finds no material errors.

skill: Enter the Research inputs in the Tariff-Impact Model
what_good_looks_like: Enters the WHAT inputs (HTS, countries, rates, dates, stacking rules, sources) in the shared Tariff-Impact Model and hands off to Standard Cost with no more than one clarification round.

skill: Run an ad-hoc investigation
what_good_looks_like: Frames the question, gathers sources and data, states the finding and a recommendation in a short write-up, and closes the Jira item after review with no material errors.

skill: Run the Research cycle end to end under maker-checker
what_good_looks_like: Takes a live tariff action from Jira intake through brief, model inputs, handoff to Standard Cost and business communication as maker, with a documented checker sign-off before release.

skill: Explain standard costing and Oracle cost elements
what_good_looks_like: Explains how standard cost values inventory and drives PPV and margin, which cost elements hold price, freight, duty and fees in [COMPANY: Oracle EBS or Fusion], and when standards are changed.

skill: Build item landed cost
what_good_looks_like: Rebuilds an item's landed cost from source data (price, freight, insurance, duty, MPF and HMF, brokerage, inland freight, [COMPANY: other components]) and matches the current standard within [COMPANY: tolerance] or explains each difference.

skill: Query item cost and cost-element data
what_good_looks_like: Without help, pulls item standard cost and cost-element history from [COMPANY: warehouse cost tables or Oracle extract] and reconciles a sample item's total to Oracle.

skill: Model tariff impact on landed cost and margin
what_good_looks_like: Using a Tariff-Impact Brief, applies its rates and stacking to the in-scope items' duty base in the shared model, calculates landed-cost and margin impact on a stated volume basis, and passes checker review.

skill: Run the standard cost update cycle with Finance
what_good_looks_like: Follows docs/templates/domain/standard-cost-update-checklist.md to prepare and tie out the duty and landed-cost input file, gets Finance and checker sign-off before any Oracle load, and reconciles after the update.

skill: Analyze purchase price variance (PPV)
what_good_looks_like: For a closed period, explains the top 10 PPV items by driver (vendor price, duty or tariff, freight, FX, other) and ties total PPV to [COMPANY: Finance PPV report or GL account] within [COMPANY: tolerance].

skill: Explain how trade outcomes change item cost
what_good_looks_like: Explains how a USMCA claim, a classification or valuation change, or a new tariff flows into duty, landed cost and margin, including the cost effect of a denied USMCA claim.

skill: Inventory a custom tool
what_good_looks_like: Completes a Tool Inventory row (purpose, users, stack, location, data sources, run frequency, knowledge holder, risk, e2open impact) from a walkthrough or the tool itself, and the Manager confirms it is accurate.

skill: Run and support the owned tool
what_good_looks_like: Runs the owned tool on schedule without help, recovers from its known failure modes, and is the named first point of contact in the Tool Inventory and OneNote.

skill: Document the owned tool
what_good_looks_like: Publishes a tool doc (docs/templates/knowledge/tool-doc.md) covering purpose, inputs, outputs, logic, dependencies, hard-coded values, backup location and e2open disposition that the Manager could follow alone.

skill: Troubleshoot and change the owned tool
what_good_looks_like: Reads the tool's Python, VBA, Access or Power Automate logic to find the cause of an issue, and makes or triages a fix through a change request with a test and the Manager as checker.

skill: Learn a second custom tool
what_good_looks_like: Runs a second tool from its tool doc, corrects gaps in that doc, and can stand in as backup for the other hire's owned tool.

skill: Explain the US export compliance framework
what_good_looks_like: Explains EAR jurisdiction and classification (ECCN or EAR99), why license determinations stay with the Senior, EEI filing in AES under the FTR, Schedule B and the USPPI role, and restricted party screening at awareness level.

skill: Complete an exports backlog item
what_good_looks_like: Completes a low-risk exports item (data correction, master-data update, reconciliation or documentation) as maker with the Senior as checker, and adds the steps to the exports SOP draft.

skill: Check export data quality
what_good_looks_like: Profiles export records for missing or invalid Schedule B, ECCN or EAR99, country, value or USPPI data, and logs each issue with evidence and a proposed fix.

skill: Explain the report inventory
what_good_looks_like: For each report in the Senior's inventory, states its source, refresh schedule, consumers and known issues, and who to tell when it breaks.

skill: Complete a reporting backlog item
what_good_looks_like: Delivers a Power BI fix, new measure or warehouse view change as maker, compares before-and-after totals, and demos it to the Senior for checker sign-off.

skill: Explain US duty drawback
what_good_looks_like: Explains the main drawback types under 19 CFR Part 190 (manufacturing, unused merchandise, rejected merchandise) and which import, export and inventory records a claim relies on.

skill: Protect drawback data in our processes
what_good_looks_like: Names the import and export data fields drawback depends on, explains why USMCA limits drawback on goods exported to Canada or Mexico, and flags process or system changes that could break a claim.

skill: Work as a core BSA on the e2open project
what_good_looks_like: Explains the project's scope, timeline and BSA deliverables, attends sessions with prepared drafts and questions, and keeps own project items current in Jira.

skill: Map own process data to e2open
what_good_looks_like: Maps each source field for own process (AS400, Excel, Oracle, external) to its e2open concept, logs data-quality issues, and lists cleansing candidates for Manager and Senior review.
